title: Part of the day and the time

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian often puts the part of the day before the time instead of saying a.m. or p.m.: *Reggel hét óra van.* *Délben tizenkét óra van.* *Délután négy óra van.* *Este nyolc óra van.* *Éjjel egy óra van.* It works with half and quarter hours too: *Reggel fél nyolc van.* Two useful words: *korán* “early” and *későn* “late”.

sections.title: Part of the day and the clock
rows: It is seven o’clock in the morning.
It is twelve o’clock at noon.
It is four o’clock in the afternoon.
It is eight o’clock in the evening.
It is one o’clock at night.

items.english: In the morning we wake up early.
In the evening we rest late.

sections.content: *Délben* is only for noon. For the rest of the afternoon, say *délután*; for the small hours, *éjjel*.
